title: Semen Analysis (WHO 2021) and Sperm Function Tests
subject: ss-reproductive-medicine
refs: WHO Laboratory Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human Semen 6th Edition (2021)

steps.say: Diagnostic andrology begins with meticulous pre analytical specimen collection. Standardized conditions ensure reproducibility across laboratories. Deviations in delivery timing distort liquefaction and motility readings.
steps.tx: Per **WHO 2021** sixth edition criteria, a valid **abstinence period** spans strictly 2 to 7 days. The specimen must be produced via masturbation without cytotoxic lubricants, maintained near 37 degrees Celsius, and assessed within 60 minutes of collection following complete enzymatic **liquefaction**. Comprehensive clinical evaluation and disciplined reproductive management ensure optimal procedural outcomes and diagnostic precision across advanced subfertility protocols.

steps.say: The sixth edition manual revised global lower reference limits based on fertile populations. Five key quantitative parameters govern standard macroscopic and microscopic evaluation. Values falling beneath the fifth percentile define clinical subfertility.
steps.tx: The **WHO 2021 reference limits** define the lower fifth percentile thresholds for fertile couples: **semen volume** 1.4 mL, **total sperm count** 39 million per ejaculate, and **sperm concentration** 16 million/mL. Comprehensive clinical evaluation and disciplined reproductive management ensure optimal procedural outcomes and diagnostic precision across advanced subfertility protocols.

steps.say: Strict morphological criteria separate fertile populations from dysmorphic cohorts. Kruger scoring requires assessing head, neck, and tail structures under oil immersion. Borderline features are counted as abnormal.
steps.tx: Assessment of **motility limits** per WHO 2021 establishes **total motility** at 42 percent and **progressive motility** at 30 percent. Under **Kruger strict criteria** for **sperm morphology**, a cutoff of 4 percent **normal forms** separates normal samples from teratozoospermia, guiding fertility decisions. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.

steps.say: Low sample volume requires differential analysis to uncover anatomical or neurogenic obstacles. Absence of seminal vesicle secretions produces acidic anejaculation or low volume samples. Fructose testing confirms glandular contribution.
steps.tx: An ejaculate volume under 1.4 mL accompanied by an **acidic pH** (<7.0) and azoospermia constitutes severe dysfunction. Complete absence of **seminal fructose** confirms **CBAVD** (congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens) or complete ejaculatory duct obstruction from absent seminal vesicle fluid. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.

steps.say: High round cell counts in the ejaculate mandate immediate differentiation. Polymorphonuclear leukocytes must not be confused with immature spermatogenic cells. The peroxidase test provides decisive chemical differentiation.
steps.tx: The presence of **leukocytospermia** (or **pyospermia threshold**) is defined by **peroxidase-positive** white blood cells exceeding 1.0 million/mL. Using peroxidase staining to separate leukocytes from immature germ cells, counts over 1.0 million/mL indicate significant genital tract inflammation. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.

steps.say: Standard semen parameters often fail to capture genomic integrity. Double and single strand DNA breaks impair embryonic cleavage and blastocyst development. Specialized chromatin tests quantify fragmentation.
steps.tx: A **sperm DNA fragmentation index** over **30 percent** on TUNEL, SCSA, or Halo assay reflects impaired chromatin integrity. Elevated **DFI threshold** correlates with reduced natural fecundity, recurrent embryonic arrest, and early pregnancy loss, guiding the transition from intrauterine insemination to ICSI. Comprehensive clinical evaluation and disciplined reproductive management ensure optimal procedural outcomes and diagnostic precision across advanced subfertility protocols.

steps.say: Compromised blood testis barriers allow systemic immune exposure to sperm autoantigens. Circulating antibodies attach directly to the outer surface of moving cells. Agglutination hinders cervical mucus penetration.
steps.tx: Clinical **antisperm antibodies** are confirmed by the **direct Immunobead test** or MAR test. When **50 percent** or more of motile sperm demonstrate bead binding, significant immunological subfertility is present, prompting sperm processing with intrauterine insemination or ICSI to bypass the hostile barrier. Comprehensive clinical evaluation and disciplined reproductive management ensure optimal procedural outcomes and diagnostic precision across advanced subfertility protocols.

steps.say: Vitality assays become essential when spermatozoa show complete immobility. Differentiating dead cells from live paralyzed cells dictates whether assisted fertilization is feasible. Dye exclusion methods provide instant discrimination.
steps.tx: Assessing **sperm viability** separates necrozoospermia from living immotile sperm with ciliary dyskinesia. A viability threshold of 54 percent live spermatozoa is established using **eosin-nigrosin** dye exclusion or the **hypo-osmotic swelling** test, identifying membrane-intact viable sperm for ICSI. Structured diagnostic algorithms and evidence-based reproductive protocols guide tailored clinical interventions across modern fertility management.
